findings.description: The RDS instance sets storage_encrypted = false, so the database files, automated backups, and snapshots are stored unencrypted. Anyone with access to the underlying storage or a snapshot can read the data directly.

publicly_accessible = true assigns the RDS instance a public IP and DNS name reachable from outside the VPC. Combined with the database security group, this exposes the MySQL listener to network-based attack from the internet.

The database password is interpolated from var.password into the EC2 user_data script and written to /var/www/inc/dbinfo.inc in plaintext. Anyone with ec2:DescribeInstanceAttribute, access to the instance, or the instance metadata/user-data path can retrieve the live database credential.

user_data embeds the RDS endpoint, username 'admin' and the plaintext password into an instance-startup script. User data is readable by anyone holding describe permissions on the instance, which is a far wider audience than the secret store, and it also persists in the instance's launch configuration history.

The master username is the default administrative name 'admin' rather than a unique, non-guessable identifier. Default admin account names are a known credential-guessing target and should not survive into deployed infrastructure.

The policy grants s3:*, ec2:* and rds:* on Resource "*", which is effectively full administrative access to storage, compute, and database services account-wide. A compromise of the web server becomes full account compromise, including the ability to read or delete every S3 object and RDS snapshot.

The catalog app instance does not require the instance metadata service v2 (http_tokens = "required"), leaving IMDSv1 enabled. An SSRF in the PHP application would then permit unauthenticated retrieval of the instance role credentials, which as noted above are account-wide administrative.

The ingress rule admits MySQL (3306) from the entire VPC CIDR rather than from the application security group, so any host in the VPC — including other tenants' instances or a compromised non-database workload — can reach the database directly.

password = var.password writes the master password in plaintext into Terraform state, and the lifecycle ignore_changes = ["password"] block means the password is never rotated through code. Terraform state must then be treated as a secret store, and the credential has no rotation path.

The database security group allows all protocols and all ports to 0.0.0.0/0. Unrestricted outbound access gives a compromised database instance a direct data-exfiltration and command-and-control channel.

The AMI data source filters on a name containing the literal string 'portal-disk' rather than a vetted, owner-verified image, and the instance does not use IMDSv2. Pulling an image by a loose name pattern allows an unintended or hijacked image to satisfy the filter.
